clue.text: Feeling love in little ways

indicators.note: one word sits in another, so it is placed inside the other's letters

blocks.note: paths are small, narrow ways
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone senses affection expressed through small gestures.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside PATHS to give PATHOS; love as O comes from the nil score in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality that arouses pity or sadness, an emotional tone or sentiment.

clue.text: Skills he requires to make a suit

indicators.note: the answer needs those two letters added before it to become the longer word, so they are the part removed

blocks.note: hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of cards
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tailor needs particular talents to make a suit of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The tailor picture misleads: suit means one of the four sets in a pack of playing cards, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Arts are crafts or abilities, as in the arts of persuasion, so they are skills.

clue.text: It may make one smart, top or bottom

definitions.text: It may make one smart, top or bottom

blocks.clueFragment: It may make one smart, top or bottom
blocks.note: surface reading: something that smartens someone up from head to toe
setter's reading: it tidies the hair on top, or, used for a spanking, makes the backside sting

explanation.walkthrough: Smart has two senses here: neat in appearance, and stinging with pain.
explanation.definitionFit: This grooming tool tidies the head, and was traditionally also used to spank children.

clue.text: A flicker of light?

blocks.note: surface reading: a brief unsteady gleam
setter's reading: a flicker is something that flicks, here the device you flick to turn a lamp on

explanation.walkthrough: Flicker is read as a noun for a thing that flicks; a switch is also a whippy cane that is flicked.
explanation.definitionFit: The device on the wall you flick to put a lamp on or off is the toggle for lighting.

clue.text: Jolly occasion, long overdue

blocks.note: first meaning: a spell of great fun and enjoyment
second meaning: as in 'it's about time something happened'

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a party that is late; the two halves are separate meanings of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollicking good party is a high time, and saying it is high time means something should already have happened.

clue.text: How a top executive should be?

definitions.text: How a top executive should be?

blocks.clueFragment: How a top executive should be?
blocks.note: surface reading: the competence expected of a senior boss
setter's reading: a top executive is high up, so their efficiency should be lofty too

explanation.walkthrough: The joke lies in the word top: someone high in the company is expected to be high in competence.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior manager should work with great competence and productivity, and the phrase plays on their elevated rank.

clue.text: He is likely to add barrels to his stocks

definitions.text: He is likely to add barrels to his stocks

blocks.clueFragment: He is likely to add barrels to his stocks
blocks.note: surface reading: a brewer or merchant building up an inventory of casks
setter's reading: barrels and stocks are parts of firearms, fitted together by the craftsman who makes them

explanation.walkthrough: Stocks looks like a store of goods and barrels like casks, but both are parts of a rifle.
explanation.definitionFit: This craftsman builds and repairs firearms, attaching the tube that fires to the wooden butt end.

clue.text: Grasping secret societies

definitions.note: the answer is a noun: grasping implements

blocks.note: first meaning: a tool for gripping things such as coal or salad
second meaning: Chinese secret societies or gangs

explanation.walkthrough: Grasping looks like a description of greedy societies; it is a separate definition of a gripping tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongs are a gripping implement with two arms, and tongs are also Chinese criminal brotherhoods or associations.

clue.text: Hot stew taken in by medical orderly

indicators.note: stewing things mixes them up in a pot, so these letters are stirred into another order
being taken in means being received inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly takes in a hot meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Orderly looks like the hospital attendant but is the adjective; the jumbled word goes after ME of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Methodical means systematic and well organised, as an orderly person or procedure is.

clue.text: Hitting out

blocks.note: first meaning: delivering a blow
second meaning: workers who are out have downed tools in an industrial dispute

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hitting out' reads as one phrase about lashing out; split it into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking means landing blows, and workers who are striking are out on a walkout from their jobs.

clue.text: A number smash up the inn, yet set free

indicators.note: smashing something up breaks it to bits, so these letters get broken and reassembled
letters set free can wander loose and settle in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Vandals wreck a pub and somehow walk free.
explanation.walkthrough: Two indicators work on the two words, one on each: the pub is wrecked and the other word let loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is a cardinal figure, ten times nine, so it is one numeral among many.

clue.text: One, two...

blocks.note: surface reading: someone starting to count
setter's reading: the opening of a well-known nursery counting rhyme, whose next words are wanted

explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme runs 'One, two, buckle my shoe; three, four, knock at the door', so the answer is what follows the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's counting rhyme continues straight on from these numbers with this phrase about fastening footwear.

clue.text: Abused, but need it drag out like this?

indicators.note: dragging something out pulls it out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who has been insulted asks whether the matter must be prolonged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like this?' points out that the answer is the result of the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To denigrate is to belittle or disparage, so someone denigrated has been verbally attacked or insulted.

clue.text: Lover's knot, say

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the word, keeping its sound but not its spelling

blocks.note: a bow is a decorative looped knot

explanation.surface: A lover's knot is a decorative tie symbolising affection.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': the lover is a knot, said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a boyfriend or admirer, an old-fashioned word for a male sweetheart.

clue.text: A site can be created for cattle in South America

definitions.note: a descriptive definition: a place for cattle in South America

indicators.note: creating something new out of material means these letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A plot of land could be developed into a South American cattle farm.
explanation.definitionFit: An estancia is a large cattle ranch or estate in Argentina and neighbouring countries of the southern continent.

clue.text: An account that won't be overdrawn

definitions.text: An account that won't be overdrawn

blocks.clueFragment: An account that won't be overdrawn
blocks.note: surface reading: a bank account kept in credit
setter's reading: an account is a story, and one that is not drawn out at length is a short piece of fiction

explanation.walkthrough: Overdrawn is banking language, but here it means spun out too long; account means a narrative.
explanation.definitionFit: A short romantic story, briefer than a full-length book, is one whose telling is not stretched out.

clue.text: Breakfast time?

blocks.note: first meaning: a hot oat dish eaten in the morning
second meaning: British slang for a prison sentence

explanation.walkthrough: 'Breakfast time?' reads as the hour of the meal; split it into two meanings. In British slang, doing porridge means serving time in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: This oatmeal dish is eaten in the morning, and in British slang it also means a spell spent in jail.

clue.text: Cancel verbally and immediately

indicators.note: verbally means spoken out, so the phrase counts by its sound

blocks.note: to write off a debt is to cancel it

explanation.surface: Someone calls off an arrangement by word of mouth, without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: Write off and right off sound the same; the spelling the grid wants is the one meaning immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Right off means straight away, at once, without any delay, as in 'I knew right off'.

clue.text: Carve a large slice of meat

indicators.note: a slice is cut from the middle of something, so the letters are taken from within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: An instruction at the dinner table to carve a generous helping of the roast.
explanation.definitionFit: Veal is the flesh of a young calf, eaten as food.

clue.text: About to happen soon in the vicinity

blocks.note: first meaning: imminent, as in 'the hour is near'
second meaning: close by, within reach

explanation.walkthrough: One meaning is about time and the other about place, run together to read as a single phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both imminent in time and nearby in space, within easy reach.

clue.text: Newspaper article needs revision, may entail pulling out all the stops

definitions.text: may entail pulling out all the stops
definitions.note: a descriptive definition: something that may entail this

indicators.note: revising a text reworks it, so this word's letters are rewritten in another order

blocks.note: an organ is a publication speaking for a group
taken as written

explanation.surface: A journalist's piece needs a thorough editing job that may require every effort.
explanation.walkthrough: Pulling out all the stops is an idiom for maximum effort, but literally the stops are the knobs on an organ that bring in its ranks of pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: An organist playing a concert pulls out stops to select the instrument's pipes, all of them for full volume.

clue.text: Stagger out of a labyrinth

blocks.note: taken as written
a maze is a labyrinth

explanation.surface: Someone staggers dizzily out of a labyrinth.
explanation.walkthrough: Stagger looks like a verb of lurching, but it means to astonish; the answer is made out of the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To amaze someone is to astound or astonish them, which is what stagger means as a transitive verb.

clue.text: Article concerning the unknown

definitions.note: the unknown author, as credited under an unattributed text

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
on can mean about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about the unknown or mysterious.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is short for anonymous, the credit given to a writer whose identity is unknown.

clue.text: Maroon thread

blocks.note: first meaning: to leave someone stuck, as on a shore
second meaning: a single fibre or filament

explanation.walkthrough: Maroon looks like a colour describing the thread, but it is the verb meaning to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: To strand someone is to leave them stranded and helpless, and a strand is a single length of fibre.

clue.text: Phoney agent in trouble, restricting a number performing

indicators.note: something phoney is fake, so these letters are a false version reworked into a new order
being in trouble suggests disorder, reinforcing that the letters are jumbled
restricting means hemming in, so the outer letters close around another piece

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for one hundred

explanation.surface: A fake spy, caught out, is holding someone back while putting on an act.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters ENATING close around C, the Roman hundred, to give ENACTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Enacting a role means acting it out on stage, so it is a synonym for playing a part.

clue.text: Disciple to stick with the New Testament

blocks.note: to adhere is to stick fast
NT is the standard abbreviation for the New Testament

explanation.surface: A follower is urged to keep faith with the Gospels.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or supporter of a cause or teacher, as a disciple is.

clue.text: Chaperon is expected to bring the girl back

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so the name is read from right to left

blocks.note: something due is expected to arrive
a girl's name, as crosswords often supply

explanation.surface: A chaperone is meant to escort the young lady home.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman who acts as a governess or chaperone to girls, especially in Spain.
